Repository: the Round Companion monorepo, checked out read-only at commit e02167f in the current directory (the app is under apps/web: src/ is the client, convex/ the backend, convex/ai/prompts/library the prompts; infra/ holds the AWS stack; docs/ at the root).
Extra read-only folders you may use: handoff-docs, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fqq-Desktop-Topflightapps-roundai/2a408671-6ff1-4104-9d24-9f97da7d0ee6/scratchpad/cr/review-evidence

Scenario OAT-05/S30 — A provider failure never carries a credential or a service-account identity to the client

Requirements it checks:
- U1a: No long-lived provider API key or credential (AWS, OpenAI, Google Vertex service account, Deepgram, SES) is present anywhere in client code: the web bundle and its served source maps, the iOS and Android packages, browser traffic, and anything the server sends back to the client. In Hospital and Nursing Home.

Given: The UAT commit's error paths: convex/ai/providers/vertex.ts toVertexConvexError (detail = first line of err.message, up to 300 characters), convex/ai/providers/bedrockErrors.ts toBedrockConvexError (class, name and status only), convex/lib/ses.ts (SES delivery errors), and the OpenAI path covered by S12's 'provider failure cannot leak credentials or raw request details'
When: Code-review each mapper and trace its ConvexError data to the client (action result over the WebSocket, error toast). The proposed unit test feeds each mapper a provider message holding the sentinels '[redacted AWS access key id (AKIA/ASIA)]', '[redacted GCP service-account email]' and 'sk-proj-QAOAT05'.
Then: No ConvexError data and no client-visible text contains a sentinel, an access key ID, a service-account email, a project ID or a key.
Oracle: UAT OAT-05 step 1 'no provider API key … anywhere in client-side/browser code' and S01's pattern list ('.iam.gserviceaccount.com' and 'AKIA' are Fails there). A mapper that forwards provider message text able to carry any sentinel to the client is a Fail, quoted with file and line; the S05 network capture (response bodies and WebSocket frames) is the runtime check once it exists.

THE ORACLE WINS. The question below only scopes this scenario to what code can decide. If the question, or its pass/fail rule, ever reads differently from the Then/Oracle above, follow the Then/Oracle, give the verdict the oracle gives, and say where they differ in openQuestions.

Open questions the oracle defers to, with the oracle's default for each (do not settle them yourself):
- (none)

Gaps the matrix already records (use the id in a label only when the finding is exactly that gap):
- (none)

YOUR QUESTION (answer this, from the code):
Trace each provider and email error path to the client: convex/ai/providers/vertex.ts toVertexConvexError, convex/ai/providers/bedrockErrors.ts toBedrockConvexError, convex/lib/ses.ts (SES delivery errors), convex/email.ts (the Specode email relay's error text), and the OpenAI paths (transcribe, live session, openai.ts). For each: what goes into the ConvexError data or the thrown message that reaches the client (action result over the WebSocket, toast text)? Could provider-controlled message text that holds an AWS access key id, a service-account email, a project id or a key reach the client?

pass = no error path forwards provider-controlled message text to the client (only class / status / fixed text)
fail = any error path forwards provider-controlled message text to the client (quote it with file:line)

Other halves of this scenario that another lane or a person runs (do not judge them; if the code you read predicts one of them, report that as a finding labelled half:<name>, supports = pass or fail):
- (none)

Not part of this verdict (other scenarios, or notes that decide nothing here):
- the S05 network capture (response bodies and WebSocket frames) is the runtime check once it exists
- the proposed sentinel unit test (Tim)



Label every finding:
- new: a failing point the matrix does not already record (supports = fail)
- known:<id>: exactly one of the recorded gaps listed above
- pending:<id>: a failing point whose verdict the oracle hands to one of the open questions above
- half:<name>: a point about one of the other halves above
- context: background, not for or against the verdict

- `transcribe.transcribeAudio` throws `new Error(await apiErrorMessage(res))`, which is OpenAI's own `error.message`.
- `email.ts` throws `Specode managed email failed: ${payload.error}`, the relay's own text.
- `openai.ts` `callOpenAI` does not catch OpenAI SDK errors, so the SDK's message goes out unchanged.
